daily_scan.notes: First run on the six-class schema, and a one-off: the admin authorised sending the digest to a single named recipient instead of drafting it, which is a departure from the standing draft-only rule and does not carry forward. Window opened at the 2026-09-10T21:07:58Z run, so roughly 10 hours. Track A checked the 5 due records one query each on the most distinctive alias (ASC30, Zoladex, AUL009, PT403, GB-7001); 36 throttled under the quiet rule, including the 4 records promoted in yesterday baseline sweep. One new finding: Ascletis started a U.S. Phase I of ASC36 oral tablets on 2026-09-08, its fourth Phase I of the year and distinct from the two injectable ASC36 studies already logged on 2026-08-10. Dated before the window, so logged and sent as a discovered-late item rather than a headline. Typed trial_data_readout to match the existing ASC36 finding rather than introducing drift. No stage_label change: the record sits at Phase 3 on ASC30 and an oral ASC36 Phase I start does not move that. The other 4 due records were quiet -- every result returned was already in their histories.

weekly_sweep.notes: Baseline deep discovery sweep across all six molecule classes, run once to seed the tracker ahead of the molecule-class change. 17 searches: clinicaltrials.gov and Google Patents scoped per class, plus wires, Korean-language trade press and deal coverage. Four new umbrellas promoted by the admin in conversation (cspc-syh2082, zealand-petrelintide, lilly-eloralintide, adocia-adoxlong), taking the registry from 37 to 41 records. cand-2026-09-10-001 resolved as promoted into cspc-syh2082. Two new candidates queued (cand-2026-09-11-001 Appel Sauce Studios/Stanford hydrogel; cand-2026-09-11-002 Jiangsu Hengrui ribupatide, flagged as probably failing the LAI bar since every source says once-weekly). Amylin was the thinnest class before this sweep and gained two of the four new records. Not logged: a Korean trade summary that Peptron has filed PT403 patents in about 20 countries targeting 2030 approval -- no publication date could be pinned, so it was left out rather than dated to the sweep.
